candidates.summary: titleKey lowercases before folding, so the Greek capitals Nu, Mu, Zeta and Upsilon fold away from the Latin letter they look like, and an all-Greek "ΤΟΚΕΝ" registers next to "TOKEN"
candidates.failure_scenario: App A registers the title "TOKEN" (key "token"). Realm B then registers "ΤΟΚΕΝ" (Greek Tau Omicron Kappa Epsilon Nu). validText accepts it because it holds no Latin letter, so the mixing rule never fires. strings.ToLower turns Ν into ν and foldRune maps ν to 'v', which gives the key "tokev" != "token". upsert's uniqueness check passes and both listings show the same drawn title. The same holds for ZONE (key "ζove"), MINT ("μlvt") and KEY ("keu"). ADR T6 claims that Greek letters which look Latin fold "to that letter". The fold is permanent for the v0 path. Cyrillic һ (U+04BB) and ү (U+04AF) are also left unfolded.
candidates.verify_by: copy tests/b1-claims-greek-capital-fold.gno into examples/gno.land/r/gnoland/store/v0 as b1_claims_fold_test.gno, then run gno test -v -run 'TestB1Greek' . there. Expected: equal keys, and mallory-token refused with title_taken. Observed: the keys differ and mallory-token is listed. The BOX control (every letter folds correctly) passes
candidates.evidence: TOKEN: Greek twin accepted with a distinct key: "token" vs "tokev" / ZONE: ... "zone" vs "ζove" / MINT: ... "mlnt" vs "μlvt" / KEY: ... "key" vs "keu" / --- FAIL: TestB1GreekCapitalsFold; a second app took a title drawn as TOKEN: "ΤΟΚΕΝ" / --- FAIL: TestB1GreekTwinRegisters

candidates.summary: isMimic refuses only U+1D400-1D7FF, so the double-struck, script and fraktur letters of Letterlike Symbols (U+2102-2149) pass validText, although T6 says mathematical alphanumerics are refused
candidates.failure_scenario: A realm registers the title "ℤℴℴℳ" (script/double-struck Zoom) or "ℍℴℳℯ". These letters are script Common, not Latin, so latin stays false and the mixing rule never fires. isMimic covers only the U+1D400 block, whose holes are exactly these Letterlike code points. validText accepts the title, and titleKey leaves it unfolded, so it lists next to "Zoom" or "Home". The ADR's T6 and isMimic's own comment both say mathematical alphanumerics are refused, and v0 cannot be changed after deploy.
candidates.verify_by: run gno test -v -run TestB1LetterlikeMathLetters with the same artifact: validText("\u2124\u2134\u2134\u2133") and validText("\u2102\u210D\u2115") should be false; both are observed true. The U+1D400 control is refused
candidates.evidence: "ℤℴℴℳ" accepted though T6 says mathematical alphanumerics are refused / "ℂℍℕ" accepted though T6 says mathematical alphanumerics are refused / --- FAIL: TestB1LetterlikeMathLetters (the U+1D400 control did not fire)

candidates.summary: ADR T10 claims tests that try maketx run on the star functions, but no test calls Star or Unstar from a gno.land/e/<addr>/run realm, so starTarget's IsUserCall guard is never pinned against a run script
candidates.failure_scenario: In store_test.gno, every Star call is made from NewUserRealm, or from NewCodeRealm("gno.land/r/starred/bot") at line 492. The /e/ run realms appear only for Register (line 84) and Claim (line 285). If starTarget's guard were loosened to caller.IsUser(), which also accepts IsUserRun, a maketx run script could star on a user's behalf. That breaks the T8 claim that stars come from direct user calls only, and the whole suite stays green because the code-realm case still panics.

candidates.evidence: the SetRealm lines before the Star(cross calls are NewUserRealm (lines 36, 56, 355, 397, 521, 580, 585) and NewCodeRealm("gno.land/r/starred/bot") (line 492); the only /e/ realms are store_test.gno:84 (Register) and :285 (Claim)

candidates.summary: An address namespace is cut to its first 6 and last 4 runes, which hides 30 of 40 characters, while the comment and ADR §7 say a look-alike namespace is never hidden by truncation
candidates.failure_scenario: Listing A is at gno.land/r/g17zyd...9cxg/poll. An attacker grinds a key whose address matches the 4 data characters after "g1" and the last 4 checksum characters, about 2^40 key derivations, which a GPU vanity search can do. The attacker's card then shows the same "g17zyd…9cxg/poll" short path. The full path is only in the title tooltip, so the truncation hides exactly what tells the two namespaces apart.
candidates.verify_by: in a Go test in feature/store, use bech32.Encode to vary the middle data until two valid g1 addresses share the first 6 and last 4 chars (about 2^20 encodes), then assert shortPath(a+"/poll") == shortPath(b+"/poll")
